skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: T2 identifies the Committee and company as the clients, says the lawyer is not the witness's attorney and cannot give legal advice, and comes at the very start. It is missing an explicit statement that the company may waive privilege without the witness's consent.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 says the privilege belongs to the company and that the company may decide to share what the witness says, including with the government. The waiver point is explained adequately.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: Rapport and expectations are minimal. The interviewer never explains how the interview will proceed, invites complete answers, or says the witness may speculate as long as they flag it. The witness is simply told to begin.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T2 ends with 'Any questions?' and the witness answers in T3. But when the witness says he may want his own counsel, the interviewer does not respond to that in T4.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T150 asks whether there is anything else the Committee should know, T152 asks about other witnesses, and T158 asks the witness to keep documents and not discuss the interview. Next steps and record retention are only partly covered.

moments.text: We represent the Committee and the company, not you personally. We're not your attorney and can't give you legal advice.
the privilege belongs to the company, and the company may decide to share what you tell us with others, including the government. Any questions?
The witness says he understands he is not the interviewer's client and mentions possibly wanting his own counsel. The interviewer does not respond to that point.
Is there anything I haven't asked about that you think the Committee should know?
Please keep any documents related to this, and don't discuss this interview with anyone.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Open invitations such as T12 ('Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999') and T24 let the witness walk through the events before the interviewer narrows.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: The interview moves from role and reporting lines (T4 to T11) to specific transactions and then to documents, which is a sensible general-to-specific order.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions are short and clear (T30, T42, T116). A few are compound or lean on the interviewer's own characterization, such as T80 with its embedded facts.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: The tone stays polite and neutral, for example 'Help me understand how those fit together' in T136. Some questions are pointed, such as T82, but they remain controlled.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: The interviewer departs from the outline when the witness raises the Fastow Family Foundation (T69 to T75) and the Kopper note (T132), and when the witness answers vaguely about the Raptor returns (T61 to T65).

moments.text: Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
Why Mr. Kopper rather than you?
What did Mr. Causey and Mr. Buy actually review before they signed its approval sheet?
How does a $4.5 million return fit with that?
It lists a $25,000 contribution from the Fastow Family Foundation. Is that the investment you mentioned a moment ago?

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: The interviewer follows up on inconsistencies: the 'stayed out' claim against the 'Andy' note (T136), the 17.95 percent versus 51 percent projections (T116 to T119), and the Board representation about the Foundation (T82).

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: The interviewer pins down who approved the payment (T140), who negotiated the buyout (T124), and what the Board was told. The when and how are less consistently covered.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: When the witness says he would need to look at the approval sheet (T53) or the investor reports (T65), the interviewer shows the LJM2 report only much later (T98) and does not pursue the sheet. Alternative refreshing paths are underused.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: The interviewer asks who set the Southampton terms (T88), but does not ask how the witness knows that Skilling approved Chewco and told the Board (T41), or the source of his understanding of the buyout price (T129).

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: T152 asks who else should be interviewed, and the witness names Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper, Andersen and V&E.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: T154 asks what documents to review, and T156 asks about personal notes, emails and files about LJM, Chewco and Southampton.

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: The interviewer follows up on 'various considerations' (T38) and on the foundation's return (T80), but does not test how certain the witness is when he says he does not recall (T45) or does not know the exact words (T147).

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: The interviewer follows up on material answers, such as the Foundation's ties to Southampton (T74 to T89), the reasons for choosing Kopper (T36 to T38), and the return on the investment (T80 to T82).

moments.text: Earlier you told me you stayed out of the Chewco buyout. This note, addressed to "Andy," refers to $10.5 million for the buyout. Help me understand how those fit together.
The Finance Committee materials show 17.95 percent. In October 2000, LJM2's limited partners were told the projected return was 51 percent. Help me understand the difference.
Who approved the payment?
I'd have to look at the sheet. Some approvals were papered after a deal closed. That happened.
The interviewer moves on to who negotiated the Raptor I approval without asking which approvals were papered after closing or pulling the sheet.
Jeff Skilling approved it. I believe he told the Board.
I understand it ended up higher. Around $10 million.
Approximately, then. Were they above or below the 30 percent the Board was shown?
Who else should we speak with to understand these transactions?
Do you have any personal files, notes, or emails about LJM, Chewco, or Southampton?
What were those considerations?
Our information is that on May 1, 2000, about six weeks after it invested, the Foundation received roughly $4.5 million on its $25,000. Is that accurate?

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.
skills.reason: The Southampton agreement and the Kopper note are introduced with context (T72, T132), and the witness confirms the Southampton document. The interviewer does not lay a solid foundation for the handwritten note.

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: Before showing the Southampton agreement, the interviewer first asks what investments the foundation made (T70). Before the Kopper note, the witness gives his account of the buyout (T129 to T131).

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: The summaries of the documents in T74 and T80 match the record: a $25,000 Fastow Family Foundation contribution and a roughly $4.5 million return on May 1, 2000.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.
skills.reason: Most document questions are open, such as 'Who approved the payment?' (T140) and 'Help me understand how those fit together' (T136). The one more pointed question, T82, is still framed as a question.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.
skills.reason: The witness gets a real chance to explain: T82 to T83 on the Foundation, and T136 to T137 on the 'Andy' note, where he says being informed is not the same as negotiating.

moments.text: What investments connected to LJM1 did the foundation make in early 2000?
I'd like to show you the Southampton Place partnership agreement, dated March 20, 2000.
Here is a handwritten note from Mr. Kopper, addressed to "Andy," that refers to $10.5 million for the Chewco buyout.
It lists a $25,000 contribution from the Fastow Family Foundation.
Michael kept me informed about things generally. Being informed isn't the same as negotiating.

missed_opportunities: T41: The witness says Skilling approved Chewco and 'I believe he told the Board,' and the interviewer does not ask how he knows or test that against the Board record.
T53: The witness admits 'Some approvals were papered after a deal closed. That happened.' The interviewer moves on at T54 without asking which approvals or showing the Raptor I sheet.
tips: When you say Skilling approved Chewco and told the Board, how do you know that, and what did you personally see or hear at the time?
Which approvals were papered after closing, and what date does the Raptor I approval sheet show compared with its closing?
